name: The Levant
story: Where the old spice routes met the Mediterranean — za'atar on breakfast bread, seven-spice on the grill, parsley piled high in tabbouleh.

name: Morocco
story: Souks stacked with cones of colour, where the spice merchant's best is called ras el hanout — head of the shop.

name: Mexico
story: Chile, lime and salt — the holy trinity of the taquería, the street cart and the hacienda patio.

name: Sichuan
story: Numbing peppercorns and star anise from the province that turned heat into an art form.

name: Thailand
story: Floating markets, roadside woks and green curry bright with basil, lime leaf and chile.

name: Northern Vietnam
story: Star anise forests in the northern hills — and the place every People of Spice jar is packed.

name: Punjab
story: Rose-pink salt hand-cut from the foothills of the Himalaya, mined since the time of Alexander.

name: India
story: Golden turmeric fields, ginger from the Malabar coast and a chai stall on every corner.

name: Sri Lanka
story: True Ceylon cinnamon — delicate, sweet bark peeled by hand and rolled into quills.

name: Scandinavia
story: Viking-era smoked salt and feathery dill — the backbone of the Nordic pantry.

name: British Isles
story: Sunday roasts, harvest suppers and buttery potatoes heaped with herbs.

name: France
story: Lavender hills and Atlantic salt marshes — the herbs and salt of the French table.

name: Spain
story: Peppers smoked slowly over oak fires to make pimentón, the soul of chorizo and paella.

name: Italy
story: From Roman arrabbiata to Neapolitan pizza and Amalfi lemons — a peninsula of perfect simplicity.

name: Germany
story: Christmas markets and Lebkuchen — gingerbread has been baked here since the 1300s.

name: Hungary
story: Sun-dried peppers strung on every porch, ground into the sweet paprika of goulash.

name: Greece
story: Oregano, lemon and olive oil — and Marathon, a town literally named for wild fennel.

name: New England
story: Home of the Thanksgiving table and the poultry seasoning that has graced it since 1867.

name: American South
story: Holiday hams, hot honey and a little heat to keep everyone talking.

name: Texas
story: Post-oak smoke, salt-and-pepper bark and the patience of the pitmaster.

name: California
story: Green Goddess dressing was born at the Palace Hotel in 1923 — herbs, herbs and more herbs.

name: Argentina
story: The Sunday asado — whole cuts over wood embers, a fire tended all afternoon.
